candidates.tagline: The pizza nobody asked for: candy corn as a topping
candidates.story: Tombstone launched a limited-edition Halloween pizza kit on October 2, 2026 — their own marketing calls it 'The Pizza Nobody Asked For' — which ships three packets of candy corn to scatter over a frozen pepperoni or five-cheese pizza, combining sweet waxy candy with hot savoury cheese.
candidates.why_funny: The company that built its brand on no-frills frozen pizza designed a product explicitly premised on the assumption that nobody wants it, then priced the horror at $1.31.
candidates.alt: A Tombstone pepperoni pizza on a Halloween-themed orange surface with candy corn pieces raining down onto the pizza from above, plastic spiders and spider webs in the background

candidates.tagline: The $720M retractable roof that ruins the game when you open it
candidates.story: During the Colts' Week 3 win on September 27, 2026, Lucas Oil Stadium's retractable roof was opened for pleasant 72°F weather, instantly flooding the field with jarring half-light and half-shadow, prompting former Colts cornerback Darius Butler to post 'boy these shadows make for a TERRIBLE tv product' — the same complaint that has dogged the stadium since it opened in 2008.
candidates.why_funny: The entire engineering achievement of a retractable roof is to let you play in nice weather — but when the Colts open theirs, the sun hits at an angle that splits the field into a dramatic shadow/glare patchwork that makes the game unwatchable.
candidates.alt: Inside Lucas Oil Stadium with its retractable roof open, bright sunlight streaming through the gap and casting dramatic shadow stripes across the field while players warm up below
